# Configuration reference

dash reads its settings from four layers; each overrides the one before it, setting by setting:
the built-in defaults, the settings saved from the UI, the config file and the environment. The
file is `DASH_CONFIG`, or `config.yaml` in the data directory. The JSON Schema of the file is
`dash config schema`; `dash config validate` checks a file and the environment without starting dash.

Every setting has a variable: `DASH_` plus its path in UPPER_SNAKE case. Lists and objects are JSON
(`DASH_PLUGINS_HARDWARE_HOSTS='[{"nodename":"pve"}]'`). Append `_FILE` to read the value from a file
(`DASH_PLUGINS_PROXMOX_TOKEN_SECRET_FILE=/run/secrets/pve`); set only one of the two forms.

A secret takes a literal, `env:NAME`, `file:/path` or `k8s:<namespace>/<name>#<key>` (the value of that key of a Kubernetes Secret,
read through the kubernetes plugin: it must run and be allowed to read that Secret; see the README). A change to a `plugins.<id>` section applies live
for prometheus, alertmanager, gatus, victorialogs, proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, flux, cnpg, rustfs, grafana, headlamp and launcher,
except for a setting marked "restart-only": that plugin restarts, and so do the plugins that use or require it
(a prometheus change restarts proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, cnpg and rustfs; a gatus change restarts hardware and
kubernetes; a proxmox change restarts hardware; a kubernetes change restarts proxmox, flux and cnpg; a grafana change
restarts alertmanager). A change to any section that is not a plugin's needs a restart, except `auth.proxy.adminUsers` and `auth.proxy.adminGroups`, which apply without one. A rotated
secret file applies live. A plugin whose `enabled` is unset turns on when it has the settings it needs, except that rustfs is off unless `enabled: true`.

## `server`

How dash listens and what it calls itself.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `server.publicURL` | `DASH_SERVER_PUBLIC_URL` | string | - | The URL people open, with scheme and host (https://dash.example.com). Required; the only Origin accepted on writes. In dev mode it defaults to http://localhost:5173 (the Vite dev server); in demo mode without dev mode to http:// and the listen address, with 127.0.0.1 for a listener on every address (http://127.0.0.1:8080 by default). _Restart-only._ |
| `server.listen` | `DASH_SERVER_LISTEN` | string | `0.0.0.0:8080` | Address of the API and the web UI. The default 0.0.0.0:8080 accepts connections from any address, so keep authentication on (auth.mode local, proxy or oidc); behind a sidecar identity proxy set 127.0.0.1:8080. In dev and demo mode it defaults to 127.0.0.1:8080, and dev mode only accepts a loopback address. _Restart-only._ |
| `server.healthListen` | `DASH_SERVER_HEALTH_LISTEN` | string | `0.0.0.0:8081` | Address of /healthz and /readyz. In dev and demo mode it defaults to 127.0.0.1:8081. _Restart-only._ |
| `server.allowedHosts` | `DASH_SERVER_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | list of strings (JSON) | - | Host names the API answers besides the host of publicURL: names or IP addresses without scheme or port. ["*"] accepts any. A JSON list in the environment. _Restart-only._ |
| `server.readyRequires` | `DASH_SERVER_READY_REQUIRES` | list of strings (JSON) | - | Plugins /readyz waits for: each listed plugin must have finished starting (its first poll or cache sync) before dash reports ready, up to readyTimeout. Empty: /readyz needs only that dash is serving and every plugin's start has returned. Names are plugins.<id> sections, e.g. ["kubernetes"]. A JSON list in the environment. _Restart-only._ |
| `server.readyTimeout` | `DASH_SERVER_READY_TIMEOUT` | duration (e.g. 30s) | `1m` | How long /readyz waits for the readyRequires plugins, counted from startup. After that dash reports ready anyway and logs a warning naming the plugins still starting. _Restart-only._ |
| `server.metrics` | `DASH_SERVER_METRICS` | boolean | - | Serve dash's own Prometheus metrics at /metrics on the health listener. Off by default. The listener is unauthenticated and the metrics name plugins and their states, so keep it cluster-internal. _Restart-only._ |
| `server.csp` | `DASH_SERVER_CSP` | string | `enforce` | Whether dash sends a Content-Security-Policy header. enforce (the default): the browser blocks what the policy does not allow. report-only: the browser only reports violations in its console, so a page that the policy would break keeps working while you find the cause. off: no policy header at all. This is the kill switch for a browser that blanks the web UI under enforce; X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy are sent in every mode. Prefer DASH_SERVER_CSP: an image rollback to a release before this setting only warns about the unknown variable, while it refuses an unknown key in a config file. In a YAML file quote the value (csp: "off"): a bare off is YAML false and is refused. _Restart-only._ |

## `server.limits`

What one client, and all clients together, may hold open or send.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `server.limits.streamsPerUser` | `DASH_SERVER_LIMITS_STREAMS_PER_USER` | integer | `16` | Open /api/v1/stream connections one user may hold; more get 429. _Restart-only._ |
| `server.limits.streams` | `DASH_SERVER_LIMITS_STREAMS` | integer | `256` | Open /api/v1/stream connections in all; more get 503. _Restart-only._ |
| `server.limits.tailsPerUser` | `DASH_SERVER_LIMITS_TAILS_PER_USER` | integer | `4` | Open plugin stream connections (the log tail) one user may hold; more get 429. _Restart-only._ |
| `server.limits.tails` | `DASH_SERVER_LIMITS_TAILS` | integer | `32` | Open plugin stream connections (the log tail) in all; more get 503. _Restart-only._ |
| `server.limits.tailMaxDuration` | `DASH_SERVER_LIMITS_TAIL_MAX_DURATION` | duration (e.g. 30s) | `30m` | A log tail ends after this long and the browser reconnects. _Restart-only._ |
| `server.limits.sseWriteTimeout` | `DASH_SERVER_LIMITS_SSE_WRITE_TIMEOUT` | duration (e.g. 30s) | `10s` | A stalled stream write fails after this long. _Restart-only._ |
| `server.limits.bodyReadTimeout` | `DASH_SERVER_LIMITS_BODY_READ_TIMEOUT` | duration (e.g. 30s) | `10s` | A request body must arrive within this long. _Restart-only._ |
| `server.limits.maxHeaderBytes` | `DASH_SERVER_LIMITS_MAX_HEADER_BYTES` | integer | `65536` | Largest request header block the API listener accepts, in bytes. _Restart-only._ |

## `auth`

How dash learns who is making a request and what they may do.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auth.mode` | `DASH_AUTH_MODE` | string | `local` | How dash learns who is making a request. proxy: an identity proxy in front of dash (oauth2-proxy, Authelia, Authentik) forwards the user name in a header, and dash believes it only from the peers in auth.proxy.trustedProxies. local: one administrator account (auth.local.adminUser) signs in at /login with a password; the first start prints a one-time setup link, or DASH_ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH supplies the password hash. oidc: users sign in at an OpenID Connect provider (auth.oidc), admitted only by auth.oidc.allowedUsers or allowedGroups. none: no authentication at all, every request is signed in as an administrator named anonymous; dash warns at every start and shows a banner on every page. It refuses to start unless server.listen is a loopback address such as 127.0.0.1:8080 (or auth.none.allowRemote is true), so keep the port reachable only from the machine itself. It is never the default. _Restart-only._ |

## `auth.proxy`

The proxy mode: which headers name the user, which peers are believed, and who is an administrator.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auth.proxy.userHeaders` | `DASH_AUTH_PROXY_USER_HEADERS` | list of strings (JSON) | `["X-Forwarded-Preferred-Username","X-Forwarded-User"]` | Request headers that carry the user name, in order of preference: the first one the proxy sets is the user. A JSON list in the environment. _Restart-only._ |
| `auth.proxy.groupsHeader` | `DASH_AUTH_PROXY_GROUPS_HEADER` | string | - | The request header the proxy lists the user's groups in, comma-separated (oauth2-proxy: X-Forwarded-Groups). Empty turns groups off; adminGroups needs it. _Restart-only._ |
| `auth.proxy.trustedProxies` | `DASH_AUTH_PROXY_TRUSTED_PROXIES` | list of strings (JSON) | `["127.0.0.1/32","::1/128"]` | The peers whose identity headers dash believes: CIDRs or IP addresses of the TCP connection (X-Forwarded-For is never read). A request with identity headers from any other peer gets 401. The default is the loopback, where a sidecar proxy connects from. A JSON list in the environment. _Restart-only._ |
| `auth.proxy.allowAnyPeer` | `DASH_AUTH_PROXY_ALLOW_ANY_PEER` | boolean | - | Allow 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 in trustedProxies. Every client could then forge an identity, so it needs this explicit opt-in and dash warns at every start. _Restart-only._ |
| `auth.proxy.adminUsers` | `DASH_AUTH_PROXY_ADMIN_USERS` | list of strings (JSON) | - | User names that are administrators: exact and case-sensitive. ["*"] makes every user an administrator (dash warns). With both admin lists empty every user is a viewer: read-only, no actions. A JSON list in the environment. Applies without a restart. |
| `auth.proxy.adminGroups` | `DASH_AUTH_PROXY_ADMIN_GROUPS` | list of strings (JSON) | - | Groups whose members are administrators; needs groupsHeader. A JSON list in the environment. Applies without a restart. |

## `auth.local`

The local mode: the one administrator account and the optional read-only access without signing in.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auth.local.adminUser` | `DASH_AUTH_LOCAL_ADMIN_USER` | string | `admin` | The name of the one administrator account; a login succeeds for this name only. Changing it after setup makes dash refuse to start until it is set back or credentials.yaml is deleted to run setup again. _Restart-only._ |
| `auth.local.anonymousViewer` | `DASH_AUTH_LOCAL_ANONYMOUS_VIEWER` | boolean | - | Let a visitor who has not signed in read the dashboard as a viewer once the administrator account exists (before setup, a visitor is sent to the setup link instead): GET requests only, never logs, never actions. Only in auth.mode=local; dash warns at every start while it is on and lists anonymous_viewer in an administrator's /api/v1/me warnings. _Restart-only._ |

## `auth.oidc`

The oidc mode: the OpenID Connect provider, who may sign in, and who is an administrator.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auth.oidc.issuer` | `DASH_AUTH_OIDC_ISSUER` | string | - | The provider's issuer URL, exactly as its ID tokens name it (e.g. https://login.example.com/realms/home). https unless the host is a loopback address. dash discovers the provider on the first login, so an unreachable provider does not stop dash from starting. _Restart-only._ |
| `auth.oidc.clientID` | `DASH_AUTH_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` | string | - | The client ID dash is registered under at the provider. Its redirect URL is server.publicURL followed by /auth/callback. _Restart-only._ |
| `auth.oidc.clientSecret` | `DASH_AUTH_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` | string | - | The client secret: a literal, env:NAME, file:/path or k8s:<namespace>/<name>#<key>. It is read at each login, so a rotated file applies without a restart. _Secret._ _Restart-only._ |
| `auth.oidc.scopes` | `DASH_AUTH_OIDC_SCOPES` | list of strings (JSON) | `["openid","profile","email"]` | The scopes dash asks for; openid is always added. A JSON list in the environment. _Restart-only._ |
| `auth.oidc.userClaim` | `DASH_AUTH_OIDC_USER_CLAIM` | string | `preferred_username` | The ID token claim that names the user. preferred_username can be changed by the user at some providers: use sub there. email is accepted only with email_verified true. _Restart-only._ |
| `auth.oidc.groupsClaim` | `DASH_AUTH_OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM` | string | `groups` | The ID token claim that lists the user's groups: a list of strings or one comma-separated string. Empty turns groups off; adminGroups and allowedGroups need it. _Restart-only._ |
| `auth.oidc.roleClaim` | `DASH_AUTH_OIDC_ROLE_CLAIM` | string | - | The ID token claim whose values are matched against adminRoles. Empty turns it off. _Restart-only._ |
| `auth.oidc.adminRoles` | `DASH_AUTH_OIDC_ADMIN_ROLES` | list of strings (JSON) | `["admin"]` | Values of roleClaim that make the user an administrator. A JSON list in the environment. Applies without a restart. |
| `auth.oidc.allowedUsers` | `DASH_AUTH_OIDC_ALLOWED_USERS` | list of strings (JSON) | - | The users who may sign in, exactly as userClaim names them. ["*"] admits every account the provider signs in (dash warns at every start). With allowedGroups empty one of the two must be set: dash does not start otherwise. A JSON list in the environment. _Restart-only._ |
| `auth.oidc.allowedGroups` | `DASH_AUTH_OIDC_ALLOWED_GROUPS` | list of strings (JSON) | - | Groups whose members may sign in; needs groupsClaim. A JSON list in the environment. _Restart-only._ |
| `auth.oidc.adminUsers` | `DASH_AUTH_OIDC_ADMIN_USERS` | list of strings (JSON) | - | User names that are administrators: exact and case-sensitive. ["*"] makes every user who may sign in an administrator (dash warns). A JSON list in the environment. Applies without a restart. |
| `auth.oidc.adminGroups` | `DASH_AUTH_OIDC_ADMIN_GROUPS` | list of strings (JSON) | - | Groups whose members are administrators; needs groupsClaim. A group added here applies at the member's next login, a removed one at once. A JSON list in the environment. Applies without a restart. |

## `auth.none`

The none mode: whether it may run on a listener other machines can reach.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auth.none.allowRemote` | `DASH_AUTH_NONE_ALLOW_REMOTE` | boolean | - | Let auth.mode=none start on a server.listen address that is not loopback (such as the default 0.0.0.0:8080). Anyone who can reach dash is then an administrator; dash warns at every start and refuses settings changes and connection tests. Without it, none on such an address refuses to start. It cannot be set from the settings page. _Restart-only._ |

## `settings`

The settings store behind the settings page.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `settings.ui` | `DASH_SETTINGS_UI` | string | `editable` | Whether the settings page may save values: editable, or readonly (fully managed, GitOps). A data directory that is missing or not writable is read-only either way. _Restart-only._ |
| `settings.secretNamespaces` | `DASH_SETTINGS_SECRET_NAMESPACES` | list of strings (JSON) | - | Kubernetes namespaces, besides the one dash runs in, that a k8s:<namespace>/<name>#<key> secret reference saved from the settings page may name. Empty: only dash's own namespace. References in the config file or the environment are the operator's and may name any namespace. It cannot be set from the settings page. A JSON list in the environment. _Restart-only._ |

## Top level

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dataDir` | `DASH_DATA_DIR` | string | `/data` | Where dash keeps its state (ui-settings.yaml, audit.jsonl) and looks for config.yaml. Demo mode uses none. _Restart-only._ |

## `ui`

What the web UI is told by the server.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ui.iconBaseURL` | `DASH_UI_ICON_BASE_URL` | string | - | Where icons resolve, for launcher links and for the apps on the Apps page: an icon called proxmox is requested from <iconBaseURL>/proxmox.png (one trailing .png, .svg or .webp on the name is dropped first), and an absolute icon URL is used only when it lies under this URL. Homepage-style names (mdi-, si- and sh- prefixes) show no icon. An http(s) URL with a host, without query or fragment, e.g. https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/homarr-labs/dashboard-icons/png. Empty (the default) shows letter tiles for launcher links and apps, so dash makes no third-party request for icons. _Restart-only._ |

## `plugins.prometheus`

VictoriaMetrics or Prometheus: the series behind charts, KPIs and host metrics.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plugins.prometheus.type` | `DASH_PLUGINS_PROMETHEUS_TYPE` | string | - | The plugin type. dash runs one instance per type, so this is empty or the section name. |
| `plugins.prometheus.enabled` | `DASH_PLUGINS_PROMETHEUS_ENABLED` | boolean | - | false turns the plugin off: its topics are removed, and the web UI drops its rail entry, palette entries, overview tiles and panels and shows a switched-off page at its address. Unset turns it on when it has the settings it needs (rustfs is off unless enabled: true, because nothing in its settings says an object store exists); a plugin without them is disabled ("not configured: set plugins.<id>.url", naming the setting to make) and the web UI hides its pages. true with settings missing or invalid makes it unconfigured, which hides its pages too. This is how prometheus, alertmanager, gatus, victorialogs, proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, flux, cnpg, rustfs, grafana, headlamp and launcher behave, and a change to any of their settings applies live: that plugin restarts, and so do the plugins that use or require it (a prometheus change restarts proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, cnpg and rustfs; a gatus change restarts hardware and kubernetes; a proxmox change restarts hardware; a kubernetes change restarts proxmox, flux and cnpg; a grafana change restarts alertmanager). |
| `plugins.prometheus.url` | `DASH_PLUGINS_PROMETHEUS_URL` | string | - | Base URL of the service, e.g. http://host:9090. Empty turns the source off: dash makes no request and its panels show "source not configured". |
| `plugins.prometheus.timeout` | `DASH_PLUGINS_PROMETHEUS_TIMEOUT` | duration (e.g. 30s) | `5s` | How long one query may take before dash gives up on it. |
| `plugins.prometheus.headers` | `DASH_PLUGINS_PROMETHEUS_HEADERS` | object (JSON) | - | Extra headers sent with every request, as {name: value}. Plain configuration, not secrets: put credentials in auth. Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie and Host cannot be set. A JSON object in the environment. |

## `plugins.prometheus.auth.basic`

HTTP Basic authentication. Not together with bearerToken.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plugins.prometheus.auth.basic.username` | `DASH_PLUGINS_PROMETHEUS_AUTH_BASIC_USERNAME` | string | - | User name. |
| `plugins.prometheus.auth.basic.password` | `DASH_PLUGINS_PROMETHEUS_AUTH_BASIC_PASSWORD` | string | - | Password: a literal, env:NAME, file:/path or k8s:<namespace>/<name>#<key> (read from that Kubernetes Secret by the kubernetes plugin, which must run and be allowed to read it). Set together with username. _Secret._ |

## `plugins.prometheus.auth`

How dash authenticates to the service. Neither basic nor bearerToken sends no credentials.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plugins.prometheus.auth.bearerToken` | `DASH_PLUGINS_PROMETHEUS_AUTH_BEARER_TOKEN` | string | - | Bearer token sent as Authorization: Bearer: a literal, env:NAME, file:/path or k8s:<namespace>/<name>#<key> (read from that Kubernetes Secret by the kubernetes plugin, which must run and be allowed to read it). Not together with basic. _Secret._ |

## `plugins.prometheus.tls`

How dash verifies the service's certificate.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plugins.prometheus.tls.caFile` | `DASH_PLUGINS_PROMETHEUS_TLS_CA_FILE` | string | - | Path of a PEM file with the certificate authority that signed the service's certificate, added to the system roots. Empty uses the system roots only. |
| `plugins.prometheus.tls.insecureSkipVerify` | `DASH_PLUGINS_PROMETHEUS_TLS_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY` | boolean | - | Skip verifying the service's certificate and host name. Anyone on the network path can then impersonate the service: prefer caFile. |

## `plugins.alertmanager`

Alertmanager: alerts and silences.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plugins.alertmanager.type` | `DASH_PLUGINS_ALERTMANAGER_TYPE` | string | - | The plugin type. dash runs one instance per type, so this is empty or the section name. |
| `plugins.alertmanager.enabled` | `DASH_PLUGINS_ALERTMANAGER_ENABLED` | boolean | - | false turns the plugin off: its topics are removed, and the web UI drops its rail entry, palette entries, overview tiles and panels and shows a switched-off page at its address. Unset turns it on when it has the settings it needs (rustfs is off unless enabled: true, because nothing in its settings says an object store exists); a plugin without them is disabled ("not configured: set plugins.<id>.url", naming the setting to make) and the web UI hides its pages. true with settings missing or invalid makes it unconfigured, which hides its pages too. This is how prometheus, alertmanager, gatus, victorialogs, proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, flux, cnpg, rustfs, grafana, headlamp and launcher behave, and a change to any of their settings applies live: that plugin restarts, and so do the plugins that use or require it (a prometheus change restarts proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, cnpg and rustfs; a gatus change restarts hardware and kubernetes; a proxmox change restarts hardware; a kubernetes change restarts proxmox, flux and cnpg; a grafana change restarts alertmanager). |
| `plugins.alertmanager.url` | `DASH_PLUGINS_ALERTMANAGER_URL` | string | - | Base URL of the service, e.g. http://host:9090. Empty turns the source off: dash makes no request and its panels show "source not configured". |
| `plugins.alertmanager.ignoreAlerts` | `DASH_PLUGINS_ALERTMANAGER_IGNORE_ALERTS` | list of strings (JSON) | `["Watchdog","InfoInhibitor"]` | Alert names dash drops everywhere: the alert list, the attention items and the firing count. A JSON list in the environment. |
| `plugins.alertmanager.severityMap` | `DASH_PLUGINS_ALERTMANAGER_SEVERITY_MAP` | object (JSON) | `{"critical":"crit","warning":"warn"}` | How an alert's severity label value becomes dash's severity (crit or warn), as {label value: severity}. A JSON object in the environment. |
| `plugins.alertmanager.silenceDurations` | `DASH_PLUGINS_ALERTMANAGER_SILENCE_DURATIONS` | list of strings (JSON) | `["1h","4h","24h","7d"]` | The silence lengths the dialog offers, from 1h, 4h, 24h and 7d. A JSON list in the environment. |
| `plugins.alertmanager.protectedAlerts` | `DASH_PLUGINS_ALERTMANAGER_PROTECTED_ALERTS` | list of strings (JSON) | `["Watchdog"]` | Alert names nobody can silence through dash, whatever the role. A JSON list in the environment. |

## `plugins.gatus`

Gatus: endpoint health.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plugins.gatus.type` | `DASH_PLUGINS_GATUS_TYPE` | string | - | The plugin type. dash runs one instance per type, so this is empty or the section name. |
| `plugins.gatus.enabled` | `DASH_PLUGINS_GATUS_ENABLED` | boolean | - | false turns the plugin off: its topics are removed, and the web UI drops its rail entry, palette entries, overview tiles and panels and shows a switched-off page at its address. Unset turns it on when it has the settings it needs (rustfs is off unless enabled: true, because nothing in its settings says an object store exists); a plugin without them is disabled ("not configured: set plugins.<id>.url", naming the setting to make) and the web UI hides its pages. true with settings missing or invalid makes it unconfigured, which hides its pages too. This is how prometheus, alertmanager, gatus, victorialogs, proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, flux, cnpg, rustfs, grafana, headlamp and launcher behave, and a change to any of their settings applies live: that plugin restarts, and so do the plugins that use or require it (a prometheus change restarts proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, cnpg and rustfs; a gatus change restarts hardware and kubernetes; a proxmox change restarts hardware; a kubernetes change restarts proxmox, flux and cnpg; a grafana change restarts alertmanager). |
| `plugins.gatus.url` | `DASH_PLUGINS_GATUS_URL` | string | - | Base URL of the service, e.g. http://host:9090. Empty turns the source off: dash makes no request and its panels show "source not configured". |
| `plugins.gatus.criticalGroups` | `DASH_PLUGINS_GATUS_CRITICAL_GROUPS` | list of strings (JSON) | - | Gatus groups whose failing checks are critical (compared without regard to case); a failing check in any other group is a warning. The Status page lists these groups first. Empty makes every failure a warning. A JSON list in the environment. |
| `plugins.gatus.pageSize` | `DASH_PLUGINS_GATUS_PAGE_SIZE` | integer | `30` | Check results Gatus returns per endpoint (the pageSize query parameter); the Status page draws them as the endpoint's history. Greater than zero. |

Unset turns it on when it has the settings it needs (rustfs is off unless enabled: true, because nothing in its settings says an object store exists); a plugin without them is disabled ("not configured: set plugins.<id>.url", naming the setting to make) and the web UI hides its pages. true with settings missing or invalid makes it unconfigured, which hides its pages too. This is how prometheus, alertmanager, gatus, victorialogs, proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, flux, cnpg, rustfs, grafana, headlamp and launcher behave, and a change to any of their settings applies live: that plugin restarts, and so do the plugins that use or require it (a prometheus change restarts proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, cnpg and rustfs; a gatus change restarts hardware and kubernetes; a proxmox change restarts hardware; a kubernetes change restarts proxmox, flux and cnpg; a grafana change restarts alertmanager). |
| `plugins.proxmox.url` | `DASH_PLUGINS_PROXMOX_URL` | string | - | Base URL of the Proxmox API, e.g. https://pve.example.com:8006. Required with a token; a URL alone leaves Proxmox disabled. |
| `plugins.proxmox.node` | `DASH_PLUGINS_PROXMOX_NODE` | string | - | The Proxmox node to read. Empty is discovered from the API when the cluster has exactly one node; set it for several nodes or to skip discovery. The hardware plugin reads the host's node from the running proxmox plugin, so without hosts[0].nodename it needs Proxmox to run (url, tokenID and tokenSecret all set). |
| `plugins.proxmox.tokenID` | `DASH_PLUGINS_PROXMOX_TOKEN_ID` | string | - | API token ID, user@realm!tokenname. Proxmox runs only with url, tokenID and tokenSecret all set and is disabled with none of the token set. A token ID without tokenSecret, a tokenSecret without tokenID, or a token without url is a configuration error that stops dash at startup. |
| `plugins.proxmox.tokenSecret` | `DASH_PLUGINS_PROXMOX_TOKEN_SECRET` | string | - | API token secret: a literal, env:NAME, file:/path or k8s:<namespace>/<name>#<key> (read from that Kubernetes Secret by the kubernetes plugin, which must run and be allowed to read it). Set together with tokenID: one without the other is a configuration error. _Secret._ |

Unset turns it on when it has the settings it needs (rustfs is off unless enabled: true, because nothing in its settings says an object store exists); a plugin without them is disabled ("not configured: set plugins.<id>.url", naming the setting to make) and the web UI hides its pages. true with settings missing or invalid makes it unconfigured, which hides its pages too. ## `plugins.kubernetes`

Kubernetes: how dash reaches and reads the cluster.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Description |

| `plugins.kubernetes.type` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_TYPE` | string | - | The plugin type. dash runs one instance per type, so this is empty or the section name. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.enabled` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_ENABLED` | boolean | - | false turns the plugin off: its topics are removed, and the web UI drops its rail entry, palette entries, overview tiles and panels and shows a switched-off page at its address. Unset turns it on when it has the settings it needs (rustfs is off unless enabled: true, because nothing in its settings says an object store exists); a plugin without them is disabled ("not configured: set plugins.<id>.url", naming the setting to make) and the web UI hides its pages. true with settings missing or invalid makes it unconfigured, which hides its pages too. This is how prometheus, alertmanager, gatus, victorialogs, proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, flux, cnpg, rustfs, grafana, headlamp and launcher behave, and a change to any of their settings applies live: that plugin restarts, and so do the plugins that use or require it (a prometheus change restarts proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, cnpg and rustfs; a gatus change restarts hardware and kubernetes; a proxmox change restarts hardware; a kubernetes change restarts proxmox, flux and cnpg; a grafana change restarts alertmanager). |
| `plugins.kubernetes.mode` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_MODE` | string | `auto` | How dash reaches the cluster: auto uses the kubeconfig when kubeconfig (or the standard KUBECONFIG variable) is set, else the in-cluster configuration, else runs without a cluster (the plugin is unavailable and the pages that need it are hidden); inCluster and kubeconfig insist on that one source and report an error when it is missing. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.kubeconfig` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_KUBECONFIG` | string | - | Path of a kubeconfig file, used outside the cluster (development). Empty means the in-cluster configuration. The standard KUBECONFIG variable fills it too; this setting's own variable wins. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.context` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_CONTEXT` | string | - | The kubeconfig context to use. Empty uses the kubeconfig's current context. Only read with a kubeconfig. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.qps` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_QPS` | integer | `20` | Requests per second dash's Kubernetes client may send. 0 or unset means the default, 20; a negative value is refused. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.burst` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_BURST` | integer | `40` | Burst of requests the client may send at once, at least qps. 0 or unset means the default, 40; a negative value is refused. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.upstreamViaAPIServer` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_UPSTREAM_VIA_API_SERVER` | boolean | - | Send the requests of the other plugins to in-cluster service URLs (http://<service>.<namespace>.svc) through the API server's service proxy, with the Kubernetes credentials. For running dash on a laptop against a remote cluster (development); off by default. Applies to requests made after the plugin starts. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.backupJobs` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_BACKUP_JOBS` | list of objects (JSON) | - | The CronJobs behind the backup ages, as [{namespace, cronjob, label}] (up to 8). cronjob also matches every CronJob named cronjob-<suffix>. label names the row; empty names each row after the CronJob. Empty hides the backup rows. A JSON list in the environment. |

A trailing / is ignored. The default is gethomepage.dev. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.apps.ingress` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_APPS_INGRESS` | boolean | - | Also read networking.k8s.io Ingresses: one app per rule host. Needs get, list and watch on ingresses in the cluster role; off by default. |

## `plugins.flux`

Flux: how dash reads Flux objects.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plugins.flux.type` | `DASH_PLUGINS_FLUX_TYPE` | string | - | The plugin type. dash runs one instance per type, so this is empty or the section name. |
| `plugins.flux.enabled` | `DASH_PLUGINS_FLUX_ENABLED` | boolean | - | false turns the plugin off: its topics are removed, and the web UI drops its rail entry, palette entries, overview tiles and panels and shows a switched-off page at its address. Unset turns it on when it has the settings it needs (rustfs is off unless enabled: true, because nothing in its settings says an object store exists); a plugin without them is disabled ("not configured: set plugins.<id>.url", naming the setting to make) and the web UI hides its pages. true with settings missing or invalid makes it unconfigured, which hides its pages too. This is how prometheus, alertmanager, gatus, victorialogs, proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, flux, cnpg, rustfs, grafana, headlamp and launcher behave, and a change to any of their settings applies live: that plugin restarts, and so do the plugins that use or require it (a prometheus change restarts proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, cnpg and rustfs; a gatus change restarts hardware and kubernetes; a proxmox change restarts hardware; a kubernetes change restarts proxmox, flux and cnpg; a grafana change restarts alertmanager). |
| `plugins.flux.suspendReasonAnnotation` | `DASH_PLUGINS_FLUX_SUSPEND_REASON_ANNOTATION` | string | - | Flux object annotation whose value is shown as the reason the object is suspended. Empty hides the reason. |

## `plugins.flux.verify`

Which Flux sources must be signature-verified.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plugins.flux.verify.requireWhenSpecVerify` | `DASH_PLUGINS_FLUX_VERIFY_REQUIRE_WHEN_SPEC_VERIFY` | boolean | `true` | A GitRepository or OCIRepository that has spec.verify must report SourceVerified=True: without it the source is critical on the overview, in the verified tile and on the GitOps page. false puts only the sources listed in sources in scope, for the attention items, the tile and the page alike. The default is true. |
| `plugins.flux.verify.sources` | `DASH_PLUGINS_FLUX_VERIFY_SOURCES` | list of objects (JSON) | - | Sources that must be signed and verified, as [{kind, namespace, name}] with kind GitRepository or OCIRepository. Each is critical on the overview when it lacks spec.verify or SourceVerified=True, or when it does not exist, and each is listed on the GitOps page. A JSON list in the environment. |

The names of the Prometheus series dash reads. Each must be a valid metric name.

| `plugins.rustfs.metrics.bucketUsed` | `DASH_PLUGINS_RUSTFS_METRICS_BUCKET_USED` | string | `rustfs_bucket_usage_usage_bytes` | Series of a bucket's used bytes, labelled bucket. The default is rustfs_bucket_usage_usage_bytes. |
| `plugins.rustfs.metrics.bucketQuota` | `DASH_PLUGINS_RUSTFS_METRICS_BUCKET_QUOTA` | string | `rustfs_bucket_usage_quota_bytes` | Series of a bucket's quota in bytes, labelled bucket. A bucket without one has no quota. The default is rustfs_bucket_usage_quota_bytes. |
| `plugins.rustfs.metrics.capacityUsed` | `DASH_PLUGINS_RUSTFS_METRICS_CAPACITY_USED` | string | `rustfs_cluster_capacity_used_bytes` | Series of the cluster's used bytes. The default is rustfs_cluster_capacity_used_bytes. |
| `plugins.rustfs.metrics.capacityUsable` | `DASH_PLUGINS_RUSTFS_METRICS_CAPACITY_USABLE` | string | `rustfs_cluster_capacity_usable_total_bytes` | Series of the cluster's usable bytes. The default is rustfs_cluster_capacity_usable_total_bytes. |

## Process variables

These are not settings; the config file cannot set them.

| Variable | What |
|---|---|
| `DASH_CONFIG` | Path of the config file. It must exist. Without it dash reads `config.yaml` in the data directory when there is one. |
| `DASH_DEV` | `true` signs every request in as `dev` without authentication and uses the development defaults; it only starts on a loopback `server.listen`. |
| `DASH_DEMO` | `true` serves fake data and contacts nothing; it opens no data directory. |
| `DASH_DEMO_CLOCK` | An RFC 3339 time (`2026-01-15T12:00:00Z`) the demo world stands still at, so every demo value is the same on every run (the README screenshots). Only with `DASH_DEMO=true`; dash refuses to start with it otherwise. |
| `DASH_SECRET_KEY`, `DASH_SECRET_KEY_FILE` | The key that encrypts secrets saved from the UI. Without one they can only be set through `env:` and `file:` references. |
| `DASH_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS`, `DASH_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS_FILE` | The key being rotated out. |
| `KUBECONFIG` | Fills `plugins.kubernetes.kubeconfig` (another tool's variable: no `_FILE` form). The generated name wins over it. |

The names dash read before the config file (`DASH_PUBLIC_URL`, `DASH_VM_URL` and the like) were removed in
0.5.0; dash refuses to start and names the replacement. See "Removed variable names" in the README.
